title: Prescribed separable residue extensions by finite etale local rings
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a nonzero commutative local ring, where $\mathfrak m$ is its unique maximal ideal and $k=R/\mathfrak m$. Let $E/k$ be a separable algebraic field extension [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. There exist a small nonempty directed poset $I$ and a system of nonzero local $R$-algebras $R_i$, with local injective structural and transition maps, such that every $R_i$ is finite etale over $R$ and every transition $R_i\to R_j$ is finite etale. Here finite means finitely generated as a module and etale means that the induced morphism of affine spectra is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. There are compatible embeddings $\kappa_i=R_i/\mathfrak mR_i\hookrightarrow E$, the ideals $\mathfrak mR_i$ are maximal, and $\bigcup_i\kappa_i=E$. The colimit $R_E=\varinjlim_iR_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] is a nonzero local ring, all $R_i\to R_E$ are local injective maps, its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak mR_E$, and its residue field is identified with $E$. A map of local rings is local when the inverse image of the target maximal ideal is the source maximal ideal. Moreover, suppose $R\to S$ is local, $S$ is strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and a $k$-embedding $E\hookrightarrow S/\mathfrak m_S$ extending the residue map is specified. For every $i$ there is a unique local $R$-map $R_i\to S$ inducing the specified map $\kappa_i\to S/\mathfrak m_S$. These maps are compatible and induce a local $R$-map $R_E\to S$ with the specified residue map.

source.place: Tags 09E0 (lemma-colimit-finite-etale-given-residue-field), local finite-etale system, and 04GT (lemma-strictly-henselian-functorial-prepare), uniqueness of residue-compatible target maps; maximal ideals and local colimit assertions make explicit the local system in 09E0.

proof.text: First give the successor construction. Suppose $A$ is nonzero local with residue field $k\subseteq F\subseteq E$, and $x\in E$. Its minimal polynomial $p\in F[T]$ is monic of positive degree and $F[T]/(p)=F(x)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-polynomial-quotient-field-iso]. It is separable by [lem-sfb-separable-algebraic-intermediate-base] and [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Lift its coefficients to a monic $f\in A[T]$ and put $B=A[T]/(f)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], $B$ is finite free with basis $1,T,\ldots,T^{\deg p-1}$, the map $A\to B$ is injective, and $B/\mathfrak m_AB=F(x)$ with its specified embedding in $E$.

source.place: Tag 09E0 (lemma-colimit-finite-etale-given-residue-field), proof, using the monogenic construction and limit stages of Tag 03C3 (lemma-flat-local-given-residue-field)

proof.text: The ring $B$ just constructed is local. For each $b\in B$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-endomorphism-finite-module-monic] to multiplication by $b$ on $B$ and evaluate the annihilating polynomial on $1$: $b$ is integral over $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-maximal-contracts-maximal], every maximal ideal of $B$ contracts to $\mathfrak m_A$, and hence contains $\mathfrak m_AB$. The quotient is the field $F(x)$, so this is the unique maximal ideal. The map $A\to B$ is local. Coprimality of $p,p\prime$ means that the class of $f\prime$ in $B/\mathfrak m_AB$ is invertible [def-pc-separable-polynomial]; thus $f\prime$ is a unit of the local ring $B$. Consequently $B$ equals its localization at $f\prime$, and [lem-weil-pbc-standard-etale-monic-derivative] makes $A\to B$ etale. This proves every assertion about the successor map, without assuming $A$ henselian.

source.place: Tag 09E0 (lemma-colimit-finite-etale-given-residue-field), proof, using the monogenic construction and limit stages of Tag 03C3 (lemma-flat-local-given-residue-field)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-well-ordering-theorem] and [lem-trf-well-order-ordinal-enumeration], enumerate the underlying set of $E$ as $(x_\alpha)_{\alpha<\theta}$ for a set-sized ordinal $\theta$. Use [lem-weil-pbc-transfinite-recursion] to construct a continuous tower starting at $A_0=R$: at successor $\alpha+1$ apply steps 1--2 to $A_\alpha$ and $x_\alpha$; at a nonzero limit take the ring direct limit with its canonical maps. Inductively the maps are injective and local, $A_\alpha$ has maximal ideal $\mathfrak mA_\alpha$, and a residue map $\psi_\alpha:A_\alpha\to E$ has this kernel and field image $F_\alpha$. At a limit this is verified directly: represent elements at stages and identify two representatives when they agree later; injectivity lets us regard the colimit as a union. An element outside the union of the stage maximal ideals has an inverse at its own stage, while an element in that union maps to zero in $E$ and cannot be a unit. That union is exactly $\mathfrak mA_\lambda$, since ideal expressions use finitely many elements and thus belong to one stage. Its quotient is the union of the $F_\alpha$. Successor injectivity is the power-basis assertion of step 1, and successor maximal-ideal equality is step 2. Thus induction supplies all invariants also at $\theta$. The image of $\psi_\theta$ contains every $x_\alpha$, so $A=A_\theta$ has residue field exactly $E$.

source.place: Tag 09E0 (lemma-colimit-finite-etale-given-residue-field), proof, using the monogenic construction and limit stages of Tag 03C3 (lemma-flat-local-given-residue-field)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-transfinite-finite-etale-union] to the tower: it is set-sized, all successor maps are finite etale by steps 1--2, every transition is injective by step 3, and the limit-stage cocones are the required colimits. Let $I$ be the set of finite-etale $R$-subalgebras $B\subseteq A$, ordered by inclusion, and put $R_i=B_i$. It is a small nonempty directed poset and its union is $A$. The structural and transition maps are injective inclusions. If $B_i\subseteq B_j$, a finite list generating $B_j$ as an $R$-module also generates it as a $B_i$-module. Both affine spectra are etale over $\operatorname{Spec}R$, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](3) makes $B_i\to B_j$ etale. Thus every transition is finite etale.

source.place: Tag 09E0 (lemma-colimit-finite-etale-given-residue-field), proof, using the monogenic construction and limit stages of Tag 03C3 (lemma-flat-local-given-residue-field)

proof.text: Each $B_i$ is local, with local map into $A$. Indeed, for every $a\in A$, choose a finite-etale $R$-subalgebra containing it. The multiplication-endomorphism argument of step 2, using [lem-weil-pbc-endomorphism-finite-module-monic], shows that $a$ is integral over $R$, and hence over $B_i$ by the same monic equation. For any maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $B_i$, [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over] gives a prime of $A$ above it, and [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal] makes that prime maximal. Since $A$ is local, it must be $\mathfrak m_A$; hence $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m_A\cap B_i$. This proves uniqueness of the maximal ideal and locality. The same argument applied to $R\subseteq B_i$ (or the known local composite $R\to A$) shows its contraction to $R$ is $\mathfrak m$, so $R\to B_i$ is local. Nonzeroness follows from the injection $R\hookrightarrow B_i$.

source.place: Tag 09E0 (lemma-colimit-finite-etale-given-residue-field), proof, using the monogenic construction and limit stages of Tag 03C3 (lemma-flat-local-given-residue-field)

proof.text: Now identify the maximal ideal of $B_i$. Its closed fibre $C_i=B_i/\mathfrak mB_i=k\otimes_R B_i$ is etale over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change]. It is nonzero and local, since $\mathfrak mB_i$ is contained in the maximal ideal just found. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product], $C_i$ is a finite product of finite separable fields. A nonzero local product of fields has exactly one factor: if there were two, the idempotent with coordinates $1,0,\ldots$ would have neither itself nor its complement a unit, contradicting locality. Thus $C_i$ is a field and $\mathfrak mB_i=\mathfrak m_{B_i}$. Restrict $\psi_\theta$ to $B_i$ to obtain the embedding $\kappa_i=C_i\hookrightarrow E$, with kernel $\mathfrak m_A\cap B_i=\mathfrak mB_i$. They are compatible and their union is $E$, since $A=\bigcup_iB_i$ and $\psi_\theta$ is surjective. All transition maps are local because contraction of $\mathfrak m_A$ through inclusions is transitive.

source.place: Tag 09E0 (lemma-colimit-finite-etale-given-residue-field), proof, using the monogenic construction and limit stages of Tag 03C3 (lemma-flat-local-given-residue-field)

proof.text: The ring $A$ is the colimit of the inclusion system $(B_i)$: for a compatible family of ring maps, define its value on $a\in A$ using any $B_i$ containing $a$. Directedness gives agreement of choices and preservation of addition and multiplication at a common stage; uniqueness follows from the union. Therefore identify $R_E=\varinjlim_iB_i$ with $A$. Step 3 gives nonzeroness, maximal ideal $\mathfrak mR_E$ and residue field $E$; steps 4--6 give local injective coprojections. This also proves the colimit assertion as an $R$-algebra, since the constructed map preserves the structural map from $R$.

source.place: Tag 09E0 (lemma-colimit-finite-etale-given-residue-field), proof, using the monogenic construction and limit stages of Tag 03C3 (lemma-flat-local-given-residue-field)

proof.text: Finally let the target $S$ and the specified embedding $E\hookrightarrow S/\mathfrak m_S$ be as in the statement. Strict henselianity implies henselianity by [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit] to the single etale algebra $B_i$, the prime $\mathfrak mB_i$, and the specified residue map $\kappa_i\hookrightarrow E\hookrightarrow S/\mathfrak m_S$. The inverse image of $\mathfrak m_S$ in $R$ is $\mathfrak m$ because $R\to S$ is local; the residue-field map is a $k$-map by hypothesis. The lemma gives exactly one local residue-compatible $R$-map $h_i:B_i\to S$. For $i\leq j$, $h_j|_{B_i}$ is local and induces the same residue map as $h_i$, so uniqueness implies equality. The colimit property now gives $h:R_E\to S$. For $a\in B_i$, $h(a)\in\mathfrak m_S$ iff $a\in\mathfrak mB_i$; as these ideals have union $\mathfrak mR_E$, $h$ is local. Reduction agrees with the specified embedding on every $\kappa_i$, hence on their union $E$.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09E0, proof via 03C3; residue-compatible maps via 08HQ/08HR (the general input to 04GT).

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q130-98968eca9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Shape: one commit; report has its review section; item statement and stmt_deps identical to the earlier unsplit snapshot. Source read: Stacks algebra.tex 09E0 (statement and proof), 03C3 (proof, transfinite-recursion paragraph) and 08HQ through lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit. Step checks: 1, the minimal-polynomial quotient F[T]/p=F(x), separability over the intermediate field F, and the monic quotient that is free with closed fibre F(x). 2, B is integral over A; maximal ideals contract to m_A, so B is local; Up+Vp'=1 makes f' a unit, so B=B_{f'} is standard etale. 3, transfinite recursion with explicit invariants; at limits the nonunits are the union of the stage maximal ideals, which is mA_lambda; psi is surjective onto E. 4, the new node's hypotheses checked; transitions B_i to B_j are module-finite and etale by cancellation (3). 5, lying over (00GQ) and 00GS give B_i local with local inclusions. 6, etale base change and 00U3 make the closed fibre a single field, so mB_i is maximal and kappa_i embeds in E with union E. 7, the colimit universal property, correctly marked elementary. 8, 08HQ for a single etale algebra gives exactly one map with preimage mB_i inducing tau; uniqueness gives compatibility, and the colimit map is local with the specified residue map. New node lem-sfb-transfinite-finite-etale-union: statement-only, self-contained, source 09E0. True: I proved it myself by descending the finite etale successor to a finite etale subalgebra of A_alpha; faithful flatness of A_alpha over the finite etale subalgebras makes the descended algebra embed. Small cases checked: theta=0, the zero ring, first limit omega, degree-1 successors. It has no local, residue or henselian content, so it does not restate the item. Searching the whole DAG for 09E0, ind-etale and directed unions of finite etale subalgebras finds no duplicate. Batch-5 flag: lem-trf-well-order-ordinal-enumeration is a status-mathlib set-theory leaf (Stacks 05N1) with no proof_deps. It is not part of the trace formula or of Poincare duality, and no other ordinal-enumeration node exists, so the citation is accepted. The generic algebra tool_uses in split_report are accepted. No changes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_local_separable_residue_ind_finite_etale (R E : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [Field E] [Algebra (ResidueField R) E] [Algebra.IsSeparable (ResidueField R) E] : ∃ P : LocalSeparableResidueFiniteEtaleSystem R E, ∀ (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [IsStrictlyHenselianLocalRing S] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] (τ : E →+* ResidueField S), τ.comp (algebraMap (ResidueField R) E) = ResidueField.map (algebraMap R S) → ∃ (h : ∀ i : P.I, P.diagram.obj i →ₐ[R] S), (∀ i : P.I, IsLocalHom (h i)) ∧ (∀ i : P.I, (residue S).comp (h i).toRingHom = (τ.comp (P.residueEmbedding i)).comp (residue (P.diagram.obj i))) ∧ (∀ (i : P.I) (g : P.diagram.obj i →ₐ[R] S), IsLocalHom g → (residue S).comp g.toRingHom = (τ.comp (P.residueEmbedding i)).comp (residue (P.diagram.obj i)) → g = h i) ∧ (∀ (i j : P.I) (hij : i ≤ j), (h j).comp (P.diagram.map (homOfLE hij)).hom = h i) ∧ ∃ f : P.cocone.pt →ₐ[R] S, IsLocalHom f ∧ (∀ i : P.I, f.comp (P.cocone.ι.app i).hom = h i) ∧ (residue S).comp f.toRingHom = τ.comp (P.residueIso.toRingHom.comp (residue P.cocone.pt))
